title: Product Video and Photo Glossary | AIVideosUGC
description: Plain-English definitions for the product photo, video, advertising, and ecommerce terms used across AIVideosUGC and links to the pages where each term matters.
h1: AIVideosUGC Glossary: Terms for Product Photos and Videos
lead: Plain definitions for the photo, video, and ad words you will see here. Open a term when it is new, then use the linked page for the next step.

entries.definition: Credits are the points each photo or video spends. A product photo is 24 credits. A video is 24 credits for 6 seconds, 40 for 10, 60 for 15, and 120 for 30. You see the cost before you confirm. If it fails, the credits come back.

Aspect ratio is the shape: how wide the picture is next to its height. A video can be 9:16 (tall), 1:1 (square), 16:9 (wide), 4:3 (a bit wide), or 3:4 (a bit tall). Product photos are square. Pick the shape of the place you will post. Then check the edges after you download.
Duration is how long a video runs. You can choose 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. One action can stay short. An unboxing or a before-and-after needs time for both parts.

A white-background photo puts the product on plain white, with no extra items. Sellers use it as the main image on a marketplace. Start from a full, sharp photo of the product. Then check that site's current image rules before you publish.

A packshot is a clean product photo. The item stands alone, so a shopper can judge its shape and surface. It is not a daily-life scene with extra items or a person. The Every Angle template makes matching square photos of the front, back, top, or base. You need a photo of each real side.

UGC means user-generated content: a video that looks like a shopper filmed it. Here, the phone looks like it is in someone's hand. An AI actor can speak a line you write, with captions and music. The actor is fictional, so describe the clip accurately if the platform asks for disclosure.
B-roll is extra video of the product, a hand, a close detail, or an everyday action. It is not only a person talking to the camera. That video can play under an AI voice, captions, and music.

Spark Ads are TikTok ads that boost a post you already published. You can send a video to TikTok from AIVideosUGC, with an AI voice, captions, and music. In TikTok Ads Manager you still choose who sees it, the budget, and the Spark permission TikTok asks for. Keep the actor’s role clear in the ad.

Retargeting means showing ads to people who already visited your shop. That includes people who viewed a product or left items in the cart. AIVideosUGC can make the picture or video for that follow-up. It cannot see who visited, and it cannot pick the audience. In your ad account, set who to include, who to skip, the offer, the budget, and how often the ad shows.

A safe zone is the middle of a social video that people still see. The app covers the edges with buttons, captions, or the profile button. You add the final words yourself. Keep the product and those words off the bottom edge and the right edge. Then preview the file in each ad account.

A feed ad is a paid picture or video in the scrolling list of posts. You get a clear product scene, often square, with room for your message. A video can already include captions, a voice, and music. Type the exact price yourself.

Ads Manager is the page in an ad account where you choose who sees the ad, the budget, where it shows, and when it runs. You can send the file to TikTok or Meta (Facebook and Instagram) from AIVideosUGC, or download it. Type the price so it matches your store now.

A product demo is a short video of one useful action, such as a kettle pouring or a lid closing. Describe that one action. Upload a photo that shows the moving part. Then compare the result with the real product.

An unboxing video shows a package opening and the product coming out. You describe the box, the paper, the insert, and the order things appear. Your product photo keeps the item looking like yours. Music can come from the library. Add the current price after the download.

Before-and-after shows the start, then the change the product makes. It fits a change you can see, such as a drawer put in order. Describe both halves. Do not promise a medical result, a body change, or better performance unless the real product can do that.

A lifestyle photo puts the product in an everyday setting, so a shopper can picture owning it. A mug can sit beside a book. The scene comes from your product photo and what you describe. Compare the result with the real item before you use it.

An on-model photo shows clothing, jewelry, a bag, or something else you wear, on a person the tool makes. Shoppers can see how it hangs and how big it looks. The tool does not give measurements or confirm the fit. Keep your size chart next to the picture.

A flat lay is a photo from above. The product and a few extra items sit on a surface. Upload a photo of the whole product, then describe the surface and the layout. Check that every item in the picture is something you actually sell.
A swatch is a small sample of a color or surface next to the product, so a shopper can judge the shade. Make it from your product photos. Then add the color name and the price yourself.

A variant is one option a shopper can buy, such as a color, a size, a surface, or how much it holds. Upload a photo for each option. Then put each downloaded file on the matching option in Shopify or Amazon.

A carousel is several slides in one social ad. People swipe through products, angles, or options such as colors. AIVideosUGC makes each picture or video. You set the order, the words, and the link in your ad account.

A CTA, or call to action, is the short line that says what to do next, such as shop or view the product. Put that line in the spoken words or the captions. Type the date and the price so they match your store now.

AI-generated content is a picture or video the tool creates or changes. It is not a photo or video you only filmed with a camera. Check every result against the real item. A generated person is not a customer testimonial. If the app asks you to say it is made by AI, do that.

A caption is words on a video that show at the right time, or the written line under a social post. Videos can include captions. Edit them in the editor so the price, the date, and any code match your store now.
Spoken narration is the voice you hear on a video. An AI actor speaks the line you write, in the language you choose. That speech is not a customer review. You can change the voice in the editor.

A template is a ready-made setup for one product photo or video, such as a white background, an unboxing, or a short demo. Upload the product photo and follow the notes on that template. Start again when you want a different setup.

A marketplace listing is the product page you keep on a selling site such as Amazon or Etsy. That site sets the image slots and the video rules. Download the files and check the current seller rules before you upload them.
DTC means direct to consumer. The brand sells in its own online store, not only on a marketplace. Sellers use the photos and short videos on that store, in social posts, in email, and in ads.

An AI actor is a made-up person on screen who can hold, wear, or talk about a product. You pick one from the actor list, or describe the look. The on-screen person is fictional; the picture does not replace a size chart.
An AI script is the spoken line the tool writes from the product and the shopper you describe. You can edit every sentence before the actor says it. The line should only say what the real item does.
An AI voice is the voice an actor uses for the line you write. You pick the language by writing the line in it. The voice is made by the tool. It is generated audio, not a customer recording.

An API lets your other software request a product photo or a video from your account, with the same credit charges and failed-job returns you see in the app. A video is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds.

A batch is several photos or videos from one product photo. Each one can have its own scene, shape, or first line. Every one shows its credit cost before it starts. Download the ones you want, or send a finished file to TikTok or Meta (Facebook and Instagram).
The built-in editor changes a finished file without another app. You can change the spoken line, the captions, the voice, the music, and the person on screen. Then download again.
Link to video starts a video from a public product page. It uses that page's main image and product name. It does not copy prices or reviews from the page. You still pick the shape and the length.
The music library is a set of songs you can put under a product video. Swap the song in the editor. You still write the spoken line, and you are responsible for what it says.

One-click publish sends a finished photo or video to TikTok or Meta (Facebook and Instagram) from AIVideosUGC. You can download the file instead. You still set who sees it, the budget, where it shows, and the schedule in the ad account.
